Schedule Risk Analysis.

Source: R/sra.R
sra.Rd

Monte Carlo schedule risk analysis of a resource-loaded project schedule. Each iteration samples activity durations (from their distributions, or from work and sampled resource productivity), samples which discrete risk events occur and their impacts, and reschedules the network with the critical path method (optionally resource-leveled; see cpm()). The result describes the distribution of project finish and cost, how often and how strongly each activity drives the finish, the impact of each risk, and the uncertainty in the cost S-curve and resource usage over time.

Usage

sra(x, num_sims = 10000, level = FALSE, keep_samples = FALSE, grid_n = 100)

Arguments

x

A "pra_schedule" object from project_schedule().

num_sims

Number of Monte Carlo iterations. Default 10000.

level

Logical. Resource-level each iteration. Default FALSE.

keep_samples

Logical. Keep the per-iteration duration, start, finish, criticality and risk-occurrence matrices. Default FALSE.

grid_n

Number of time points for the cost S-curve and resource profiles. Default 100.

Value

An S3 object of class "sra", a list with:

total_distribution

Simulated project finish, one per iteration.

total_mean, total_sd

Mean and standard deviation of the finish.

percentiles

P10, P50, P80 and P90 of the finish.

cost_distribution

Simulated project cost, one per iteration.

cost_percentiles

P10, P50, P80 and P90 of the cost.

deterministic

The cpm() result on baseline durations.

prob_deterministic

Probability of finishing no later than the deterministic finish.

activity_stats

Data frame of per-activity results: deterministic start and finish, mean and standard deviation of duration, mean and P10/P50/P90 start and finish, criticality index, duration sensitivity, cruciality and SSI.

risk_stats

Data frame of per-risk results: probability, simulated occurrence rate, finish impact, cost impact and rank by finish impact. Zero rows when there are no risks.

risk_net_stats

When the schedule has a risk_net, a data frame with one row per network node: kind ("event" for nodes whose draws are all 0 or 1, otherwise "continuous"), occurrence and mean of its draws, finish_impact and cost_impact (mean when the event occurred minus mean when it did not; events only), finish_sensitivity and cost_sensitivity (Spearman correlation of the node with finish and cost) and rank by finish impact. NULL without a risk network.

time_grid

Time points used for the curves below.

cost_curve

Data frame of cumulative cost over time_grid: mean, p10, p50, p90.

resource_profile

Named list, one data frame per resource, of usage over time_grid (mean, p10, p50, p90) with a capacity attribute.

samples

When keep_samples = TRUE, a list of iteration x activity matrices duration, start, finish, critical, the iteration x risk matrix risk_occurred, the risk-network draws risk_net (a data frame, or NULL), and the iteration x resource matrices productivity_multiplier and rate_multiplier; otherwise NULL.

leveled, num_sims, project

Settings and the input schedule.

Objects of this class have print.sra(), summary.sra() and plot.sra() methods.

Details

Activity measures.

  • Criticality index: the proportion of iterations in which the activity is critical (zero total float, or on the driving path when leveled).

  • Duration sensitivity: Spearman rank correlation between the activity's sampled duration and the project finish.

  • Cruciality index: criticality index times duration sensitivity (Williams, 1992), which ranks activities by how much they actually move the finish date.

  • Schedule sensitivity index (SSI): criticality index times the ratio of the activity's duration standard deviation to the project finish standard deviation (PMI, 2009).

Measures based on duration spread are NA for activities whose duration never varies.

Risk measures. For each risk, the mean finish (and cost) in iterations where it occurred minus the mean in iterations where it did not; NA when the risk always or never occurred.

Risk networks. When the schedule has a risk_net (see project_schedule()), its nodes are sampled jointly with prob_net_sim() in every iteration, so risks that share a root cause occur together, and their risk_effects scale the productivity and cost rates of the resources they name. Because node statistics compare iterations where an event did and did not occur, a root cause's finish_impact includes the effects of every risk it drives, and a risk correlated with others through a shared cause is credited with part of their effects too.

Merge bias. Where paths converge, the finish is driven by the longest of several uncertain paths, so the mean simulated finish usually exceeds the deterministic finish even when every duration is symmetric. This is why a network analysis differs from summing task durations with mcs().

Time-phasing. Each activity's cost (resource cost, fixed cost and its share of risk costs) is spread linearly over its scheduled dates. Resource usage is the sum of assigned units over the activities running at each time. Both are evaluated on grid_n points from zero to the latest simulated finish and summarized by their mean and P10, P50 and P90.

Performance. Without leveling, the critical path passes are vectorized across iterations and are fast. Leveling schedules every iteration separately with a serial schedule-generation scheme whose cost grows with the square of the number of activities, so large leveled models may need fewer iterations.

The returned object carries total_distribution, so contingency() applies directly to schedule contingency.

References

Williams, Terry M. Criticality in stochastic networks. Journal of the Operational Research Society 43.4 (1992): 353-357.

Project Management Institute. Practice Standard for Project Risk Management. Newtown Square, PA: PMI, 2009.

Vanhoucke, Mario. Measuring time: Improving project performance using earned value management. Springer, 2009.

Examples

activities <- data.frame(id = c("A", "B", "C", "D"), duration = c(3, 5, 4, 2))
links <- data.frame(
  source = c("A", "A", "B", "C"),
  target = c("B", "C", "D", "D")
)
duration_dists <- list(
  B = list(type = "triangular", a = 4, b = 5, c = 9),
  C = list(type = "triangular", a = 3, b = 4, c = 8)
)
risks <- list(list(
  id = "Rework", prob = 0.2, activities = "D",
  impact = list(type = "uniform", min = 1, max = 2)
))
proj <- project_schedule(activities, links,
  duration_dists = duration_dists, risks = risks
)
set.seed(42)
res <- sra(proj, num_sims = 2000)
res
#> Schedule Risk Analysis 
#> Iterations: 2,000 
#> Deterministic finish: 10 periods (P10) 
#> Mean finish: 11.53 periods   SD: 1.189 
#> Finish percentiles:
#>    10%    50%    80%    90% 
#>  9.995 11.470 12.550 13.100 
#> Most critical activities:
#>  id criticality cruciality
#>   A       1.000         NA
#>   D       1.000      0.487
#>   B       0.728      0.521
#>   C       0.272      0.080
res$activity_stats[, c("id", "criticality", "cruciality")]
#>   id criticality cruciality
#> 1  A      1.0000         NA
#> 2  B      0.7275  0.5212753
#> 3  C      0.2725  0.0804491
#> 4  D      1.0000  0.4873088
contingency(res, phigh = 0.8, pbase = 0.5)
#>     80% 
#> 1.08829 

# A supply-chain root cause drives a labor shortage that slows the crew on
# both B and C, so one risk delays two activities through a resource.
net <- prob_net(
  data.frame(id = c("SupplyChain", "Shortage")),
  data.frame(source = "SupplyChain", target = "Shortage"),
  list(
    SupplyChain = list(type = "discrete", values = c(1, 0), probs = c(0.3, 0.7)),
    Shortage = list(
      type = "conditional", condition = "SupplyChain",
      true_dist = list(type = "discrete", values = c(1, 0), probs = c(0.8, 0.2)),
      false_dist = list(type = "discrete", values = c(1, 0), probs = c(0.1, 0.9))
    )
  )
)
proj_net <- project_schedule(activities, links,
  duration_dists = duration_dists,
  resources = data.frame(id = "crew", rate = 500),
  assignments = data.frame(activity = c("B", "C"), resource = "crew", units = 1),
  risk_net = net,
  risk_effects = list(
    list(node = "Shortage", resources = "crew", effect = "productivity",
         magnitude = list(type = "triangular", a = 0.6, b = 0.8, c = 0.9)),
    list(node = "SupplyChain", resources = "crew", effect = "rate",
         magnitude = list(type = "uniform", min = 1.1, max = 1.3))
  )
)
res_net <- sra(proj_net, num_sims = 2000)
res_net$risk_net_stats
#>            id  kind occurrence   mean finish_impact cost_impact
#> 1 SupplyChain event     0.2995 0.2995      1.425979    2690.066
#> 2    Shortage event     0.3210 0.3210      1.958019    2794.433
#>   finish_sensitivity cost_sensitivity rank
#> 1          0.4139164        0.6793854    2
#> 2          0.5851144        0.7260997    1
